questions.stem: An antifungal kills Candida by inhibiting synthesis of β-(1,3)-glucan, a component of the fungal cell wall. Which drug is it?
questions.explanation: Echinocandins (caspofungin, micafungin, anidulafungin) inhibit glucan synthase; they are fungicidal against Candida but only disrupt the growing wall of Aspergillus. A: Polyene; binds membrane ergosterol and forms pores. C: Azole; blocks ergosterol synthesis. D: Converted to 5-FU; disrupts RNA and DNA synthesis. E: Allylamine; inhibits squalene epoxidase.

questions.stem: Which enzyme do azole antifungals such as fluconazole inhibit?
questions.explanation: Azoles inhibit the fungal cytochrome P-450 enzyme 14α-demethylase (lanosterol → ergosterol), damaging the cell membrane; CYP-450 inhibition also explains their drug–drug interactions. A: Target of allylamines (terbinafine). B: Target of echinocandins. C: Blocked by flucytosine's metabolite 5-FdUMP. D: No antifungal class in the lecture targets it.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man with diabetic ketoacidosis develops facial pain, fever and a black necrotic lesion on the nasal mucosa. Biopsy shows broad, irregular, nonseptate hyphae branching at right angles. Blood cultures are negative. Besides correcting the ketoacidosis, what is the most appropriate management?

options.D: Surgical debridement plus lipid amphotericin B
options.E: Amphotericin B plus flucytosine, then fluconazole

questions.explanation: Broad, nonseptate, right-angle hyphae in a diabetic with ketoacidosis indicate mucormycosis (Zygomycetes); treatment combines aggressive surgical debridement with lipid amphotericin B (or posaconazole). Blood cultures are of no benefit. A: Fluconazole is mainly for Candida. B: Echinocandins are not active against Zygomycetes. C: Itraconazole is the usual drug for endemic mycoses. E: Induction regimen for cryptococcal meningitis.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man with HIV (CD4 count 60/µL) has two weeks of headache and fever. Lumbar puncture shows a high opening pressure, and India ink staining of the CSF shows encapsulated yeasts. Which is the most appropriate initial treatment?

options.C: Amphotericin B plus flucytosine for 14 days

questions.explanation: Cryptococcal meningitis is treated with amphotericin B plus flucytosine for 14 days, then oral fluconazole for 8–10 weeks; CSF is removed to keep pressure below 20 cm H2O. A: Echinocandins are not active against Cryptococcus. B: Fluconazole is the consolidation step, not induction. D: Extended-spectrum triazole aimed at Aspergillus and other moulds. E: Management of mucormycosis.

questions.stem: Which CSF test is the most sensitive for diagnosing cryptococcal meningitis?
questions.explanation: Cryptococcal antigen by latex agglutination in CSF has a sensitivity of >90%. B: India ink shows encapsulated yeasts but is only 50–75% sensitive. C: Galactomannan is a cell-wall antigen used for Aspergillus. D: Distinguishes C. albicans from non-albicans Candida. E: A rapid test to speciate Candida.

questions.stem: Which patient with proven invasive candidiasis should receive an echinocandin rather than fluconazole as initial therapy?

options.A: A patient with mild illness and no previous azole exposure
options.B: A neutropenic patient who is severely ill
options.C: A patient with suspected CNS involvement
options.D: A patient with asymptomatic candiduria and a urinary catheter
options.E: A young non-diabetic patient at low risk for C. glabrata

questions.explanation: Neutropenia, severe illness, or suspected cardiac valve/myocardial involvement call for an echinocandin or an amphotericin formulation first. A, E: These are the criteria for first-line fluconazole. C: Give amphotericin B; echinocandins penetrate the CNS poorly. D: Modify risk factors; it rarely requires treatment.

questions.stem: A farmer from the Mississippi valley has chronic cough and skin lesions. Tissue biopsy shows large (8–15 µm) yeasts with a single daughter cell attached by a broad base. Culture at room temperature grows a mould. Which organism is most likely?
questions.explanation: Blastomyces is a dimorphic endemic fungus of the Ohio/Mississippi valleys: mould in the environment, large yeast with broad-based budding in tissue. A: Same region, but small (2–3 µm) intracellular budding yeasts. B: Not dimorphic; capsule with a narrow pore between mother and daughter. C: US Southwest; non-budding spherules with endospores. D: Latin America; multiple buds on one mother cell.

questions.stem: During treatment of invasive fungal infection, a patient develops a rising creatinine with low serum potassium and magnesium. Which drug is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Polyene toxicity is nephrotoxicity, hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia; lipid (especially liposomal) formulations are less nephrotoxic. A: Echinocandins have a good safety profile. B: Causes bone marrow suppression. C: Causes blurry vision; azoles also cause liver toxicity and drug interactions. E: Azole toxicity is mainly hepatic and drug interactions, not renal wasting.
